mentions.name: Tornyol
mentions.description: A mosquito-killing drone that uses ultrasonic sonar to detect mosquitoes and missile control theory to ram into them and grind them in its propellers. It targets a 40-gram tinywhoop platform so it can fly safely and almost silently anywhere, functioning like a Roomba for mosquitoes. Compared to static systems or man-portable insecticide spraying, a drone can cover an enormous surface in a short time, with the goal of being competitive with insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) against malaria.
mentions.problem: Traditional mosquito-control systems (static systems, man-portable insecticide spraying) cover limited area; the project aims to combat malaria-carrying mosquitoes far more efficiently over large surfaces.
mentions.source_excerpt:
My roommate and I are still working on Tornyol, our mosquito killing drone! It uses ultrasonic sonar to detect mosquitoes, and missile control theory to ram into mosquitoes and grind them in its propellers.

Our target platform is a 40 grams tinywhoop so it’s safe to fly everywhere and makes almost no noise :). A Roomba for mosquitoes!
